In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the c2d Spitzer survey has provided a wealth of information on the properties and evolution of embedded young stellar objects, protoplanetary disks, and star-forming regions.

the gas-phase lines of the c2d Spitzer sample are consistent with a picture of low-mass young stellar objects (YSOs) embedded within molecular clouds, where the gas-phase lines originate primarily from the surrounding envelope, but with some contribution from the disk.
the gas-phase emission lines in the Spitzer IRS spectra toward these embedded low-mass YSOs are dominated by shock emission from the outflows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the H_2 and H_(2)0 emission lines are detected in 30 and 21 of the 43 sources respectively.
the gas-phase emission lines toward the embedded low-mass YSOs are dominated by the shock-heated gas.
the gas-phase emission lines in the mid-IR are not useful for determining the physical properties of embedded low-masses stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gas-phase emission lines are not reliable probes of the physical conditions of the gas.
the mid-infrared emission lines from the gas phase are not as useful as we had hoped.
the mid-infrared gas lines are excellent probes of the physical conditions in the innermost regions (r < 10 AU) of protostars.
